doc.title: Bill Goodwin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 28, 2025

title: Recording acoustic bass: Manfred Eicher, Charlie Haden and Tom Harrell
summary: Miking the bass, Haden complaining about the Tom Harrell record's bass level, and early Danilo Perez.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Did you like to see the bass being recorded in a certain fashion? The acoustic bass?

Well yeah. Like you know several different things. One would be just stereo, a pair of mics. This is the way Manfred Eicher did everything with, you know everything in stereo. Two mics on each horn, two mics on the bass, and then more mics on the drums of course. And I had seen him do that in the studio. And let me see now. I like, you know I like the natural sound of the bass. Not all basses sound the same. Not all bass players hear their bass in the same way that I do either. For example when I was doing a Tom Harrell record I had hired Charlie Haden for it. Charlie loved to dominate the sound. And so the record came out, a very nice record. And I ran into him in some club somewhere and I said, “Did you hear the record?” He said, “Yeah. The bass isn’t loud enough.” I said, “Listen man, this here is not your record, it’s Tom’s record, and I can hear every note you’re playing. Because Charlie couldn’t really read and he was really roughing it off there quite a bit.

It might have helped. The music was fine. There was one called “Form.” It was also on Contemporary Records as a matter of fact. It was owned by Fantasy at that point. And I got to record a bunch of Tom’s records for them and then later the Chesky Brothers, Chesky Records with Tom. But you know Paul Motian and Danilo Perez — early recording of Danilo — he wasn’t even 21 yet.
Yeah he was pretty great, man. I just loved that guy.
